title: Kennedy Center begins removal of outdoor ‘Blue’ sculpture | CNN Politics
text:
Source: CNN

The Kennedy Center has taken down a stick figure sculpture on the grounds as President Donald Trump has aimed to reshape the performing arts institution, including with new art.

The National Park Servicetemporarily closeda road for several hours for the statue’s removal as cranes removed large pieces of the sculpture.

Called “Blue,” from the artist Joel Shapiro, the statue depicts a stick figure “mid-kick.” It wasinstalled outside the Kennedy Center in 2019.

A Kennedy Center spokesperson said in a statement to CNN that the venue requested the “deinstallation,” which the person described as “common practice.”

“We are deeply grateful to Joel Shapiro for the yearsBluehas spent animating our campus and connecting visitors to his vision,” the spokesperson said. “We are honored to have been stewards of his vibrant work and a part of his enduring legacy.”

A former curator for the institution, Josef Palermo, told CNN that in September 2025, he was told to remove all of the outdoor art, including “Blue,” as the president wanted “all new art for the reopening.” CNN has reached out to the White House for comment. A person familiar with the matter denied Palermo’s account of the situation.

Since President Donald Trump returned to the White House last year, he has made several moves to reshape the Kennedy Center, including hand picking the center’s board of trustees and beingelectedits chair. The board later voted to add his name to the building, an effort that faced legal challenges.

The activist organization “Hands Off the Arts” described the sculpture as a “beloved figure” in anInstagram postand called its removal “buffoonery.”

“Wednesday, September 2, 2026 will forever be known as the day the United States government tore down a piece of public art at the behest of a petulant crybaby,” the organization said, seemingly referring to Trump. “But it won’t be the last.”

Earlier this year, Trump announced that the Kennedy Center wouldclose for around two yearsfor renovations. It was slated to close on July 4 but a federal judge blocked the renovation plans, ruling that they were made unlawfully.

But the Trump administration and the Kennedy Center board have continued to push back on legal challenges. Last month, lawyers for the centerthreatened to demolishthe building if renovations aren’t allowed. The board has also said it will onceagain add Trump’s nameto the building.

This story has been updated with additional information.

CNN’s Betsy Klein and Sunlen Serfaty contributed to this report.

CNN’s Betsy Klein and Sunlen Serfaty contributed to this report.
